From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>

Subject: VPC priming runbook rehearsal: telemetry, canary, and network gating

Hi team,

We’re scheduled to run the VPC/on-prem priming rehearsal tomorrow as a dress rehearsal for the cutover next week. Objective is to validate the runbook, exercise telemetry priming, and run the canary smoke tests end-to-end with Acme’s ops team.

High-level agenda (90m):
- 0-15m: Preflight checklist & ownership (ACLs, MTU, BGP/EBGP peering confirmations)
- 15-45m: KV-cache warmup + prefix cache validation (scripts attached)
- 45-70m: Canary traffic + health-checks (service & metrics verification)
- 70-90m: Post-run log collection & rollback smoke (fallback route test)

Key asks:
1) Acme: confirm firewall ACLs for Redwood egress IPs and that their NVA will not rewrite source ports during canary traffic (ops-l3 copied).
2) Stephanie: lead the metrics verification and validate that the Grafana panels in the runbook match live data.
3) Marcus: walk the curl and TCP checks in the runbook; I’ll run the orchestration steps.

Attachments: redwood_vpc_priming_runbook_v2.pdf (runbook), smoke_step_results_template.csv (results template).

Telemetry priming notes:
- Add a short spike after KV warmup to validate prefix hit-rate (5k requests to the prefix endpoint).
- Ensure telemetry retention markers are visible in the telemetry pipeline (span ids and request_id).

If all good, please reply with ‘ACK’ and any blocking concerns. We’ll target 10:00am PT tomorrow (Nov 15).

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Sr. Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Thanks — I’ll own the smoke checklist. A couple of clarifications and the commands we’ll run so Acme can sanity check on their side before 10:00: 

Preflight checks (to be run from our jump host):
- BGP session: show ip bgp summary | grep acme-peer (expect: Established, uptime > 300s)
- ACLs: tcpdump -n -i eth0 port 443 and confirm no rewrite of src port
- MTU: ping -M do -s 8972 <acme-probe-ip> (expect no fragmentation)

Smoke commands (in runbook order):
1) KV warmup: python scripts/kv_warmup.py --host https://kv-prime.redwood.internal --requests 5000 --concurrency 50
2) Health check: curl -sS -D - https://service-canary.redwood.internal/health | head -n 15
   Expected body: {"status":"ok","kv_prefix_hits":">90%"}
3) End-to-end trace: curl -sS -H 'x-request-id: runrehearsal-<timestamp>' https://service-canary.redwood.internal/api/v1/ping
   Verify trace id in Grafana and tracing: span shows edge->service->kv

I attached smoke_step_results_template.csv — please use that format for results. Marcus

Subject: Re: VPC priming runbook rehearsal: telemetry, canary, and network gating — post rehearsal readout

Team, post-rehearsal readout below. Short version: successful priming, one transient BGP flap at Acme edge during KV warmup that self-corrected after we reduced concurrency; logs attached.

What succeeded:
- KV warmup executed (5k requests) with prefix hit-rate at 94% after two passes.
- Health-checks returned {"status":"ok"} across canary endpoints.
- Grafana panels updated with trace and request_id markers; traces show edge->service->kv as expected.

Issue observed (action required):
- During step 2 (KV warmup, concurrency 50), Acme reported a BGP session reset (15s) on the transit edge which caused brief 502s for <service-canary>. We reran warmup at concurrency 20 and the session remained stable.
- Initial hypothesis: control-plane CPU hit on Acme edge due to high concurrent flows. Action items: Acme to raise keepalive and monitor CP CPU; Redwood to add a soft concurrency cap in the runbook (default 25 for shared-edge rehearsals).

Artifacts attached: post_rehearsal_log_bundle.zip (pcap + service logs), smoke_step_results_template.csv (filled).

Next steps / owners:
- Acme (Julian / Maya): validate keepalive and CP CPU thresholds, update ops playbook if needed (owner: Acme Ops).
- Redwood: update runbook to set default concurrency 25 for rehearsals; add an explicit BGP-watch step (owner: Marcus Lin).
- Lauren: schedule a follow-up validation in 72 hours after Acme confirms keepalive changes.

Please ACK the readout and owners. If no objections by EOD PT, I’ll update the runbook and the related JIRA (JIRA-INFRA-987).

Thanks everyone — good rehearsal.

Lauren Bishop
Sr. Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
